- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.5) or shows sharp reversal, model often underestimates downside; add 3–8% buffer to forecast for near-term drop.
- Model consistently overestimates 30-day horizon after recent price spikes; apply downward correction of 5–10% for spikes >10% from 14-day moving average.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.5/0.3/0.8/0.2), model exhibits mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast toward recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3 sentiment values are >0.5, model tends to overshoot; cap forecast at 10% below 30-day moving average of true values.
- When sentiment is flat or neutral (0.0–0.3), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 14-day moving average as baseline and adjust ±2% based on volatility skew.
